summary: OpenSSH on node1 is hardened and persistent. Only ssh-access members can authenticate with public keys; root, contractor, and password authentication are denied. opsadmin’s existing key is pinned to node2, and node3 is blocked at the network boundary. All three nodes were restarted sequentially and fully recovered.
actions_performed: Installed a validated sshd hardening drop-in on node1.
Pinned opsadmin’s existing authorized key to node2 (10.100.60.11) with restrictive key options.
Created the persistent ssh-admin firewalld zone for node2 and removed SSH from the public zone.
Verified allowed batch-mode access and all required denial cases.
Preserved prepared accounts, key material, and data.
Restarted node1, node2, and node3 individually and verified changed boot identities and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Public-key-only access for ssh-access; root, contractor, and passwords denied
evidence.summary: Effective sshd policy and direct post-restart tests prove the required authentication controls.

evidence.requirement: Pinned non-interactive opsadmin access from node2 sshprobe
evidence.summary: The authorized key is source-pinned to 10.100.60.11, its fingerprint matches sshprobe’s key, and batch-mode login succeeds.

evidence.requirement: Dedicated jump-box firewall boundary and node3 denial
evidence.summary: ssh-admin permanently exposes SSH only to node2’s /32 source; public has no SSH service, and node3 is blocked before authentication.

evidence.requirement: Prepared accounts, keys, and data preserved
evidence.summary: Accounts remain present, prepared data checksums match baseline, contractor key data is unchanged, and sshprobe key material and fingerprint survived restart.
Healthy baseline, acknowledged reboot, changed boot ID, recovered services/data/policy, allowed node2 access, and denied node3 access.
Healthy baseline, acknowledged reboot, changed boot ID, preserved sshprobe key material, and recovered jump-box access.
Healthy baseline, acknowledged reboot, changed boot ID, recovered client state, and persistent network denial.
